label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: COUNTY CHAMPIONSHIP STRUGGLES.

label: paragraph_title
text: NO NEWS OF HOBBS.

label: text
text: Little comment is called for in the latest county cricket matches to hand. Middlesex, who now seem to be in their best form, must be considered unlucky not to have forced the issue with Hampshire. Surrey and Lancashire won as expected but Kent's miserable total of less than fifty must have been a great shock for partisans of the Hop county. Kent have done very badly this year. On the other hand, Essex have maintained their earlier promise and are quite a different team from what they have been in other post-War seasons.

label: text
text: Hobbs, apparently does not like the Sussex, or for that matter, 'Tate's bowling. At any rate, he has seldom done anything big against them. His name is not in the results to-day. Accordingly those who are waiting for him to beat two records will have to wait a little longer.

text: The M. C. G. have enabled the Calcutta Cricket Club stoting that they deemed it advisable to postpone the tour in India till next year. A team was being sent out during the close-season to the West Indies. As both teams would have to be made up mainly of amateurs, the success of the West Indies tour might be affected by having to split forces for the India visit, hence the eable.

label: text

MONDAY'S PUBLIC
MEETING.

label: text
text: (T'o the Editor of the China Mail).

label: text
text: Sir,—I shall be obliged if you will do me the courtesy of printing the following letter with reference to the public meeting to be held on Monday next at 5.30:—

label: text
text: "It has been arranged for the City Hall but there are indications that this will prove too small in view of public interest in the resolutions to be proposed, if so, the meeting will at once be transferred to the Theatre Royal.

label: text
text: Amongst other resolutions concerning local matters arising out of the strike and the general crisis in China one will be specially brought forward dealing with the mistaken "Labour" and "Press" views of the situation in Hongkong and China and Hongkong legislation in particular, which it is of importance should be emphatically refuted.

label: text
text: I hope, therefore, that there will be a large meeting on Monday to endorse this resolution, at any rate, with no uncertain voice.

label: text
text: Our enemies are using insidious and ceaseless propaganda in all directions which needs counteracting as far as can be done.

label: text
text: I hope that Monday, night's meeting will, at least, do something to lay the truth before the public at home.

label: text
text: I trust that the Press here will assist that object as far as lies in their power.

label: text
text: P. H. HOLYOÁK. Hongkong, July 25.

label: paragraph_title
text: RAIN COLLAPSE

label: text
text:
ENQUIRY RESUMED AT
MAOISTRACY

label: text
text: Further details of his narrow escape were given at the resumed enquiry yesterday into the Po Hing Fong disaster by Sergt. Chesterwoods.

label: text
text: He was walking along. Cuine Road on the morning of the 17th about 9:25 when he heard a crack and a rumble, said witness. He looked round and saw a large matshed topple over towards Po Hing Kong. Practically at the same time another matshed close by toppled, steadied itself and then shipped to the ground. He ran along Hospital Road and down the steps there. He saw a temporary contractor's doorway out of which several Chinese ran, and he ran down the stairs wondering whether there was anyone in the matsheds. While he was running down the stairs the rumbling continued, becoming louder.

label: text
text: The Coroner: What was your idea in running down the steps?—I thought it was simply a matter of the matsheds collapsing, and went to see if anyone was there.

label: text
text: Witness said that looking behind him he saw that the steps were covered in debris. A wall in front

label: text
text: another wall, and slid down the debris into the Tai On Terrace. He remained at the place for quite a while, but there were no further slides of importance.

label: text
text: Capt. Arthur: When you were walking along One Road did you notice the condition of the road?—There was about two inches of water in Caine Road.

label: text
text: Capt. Arthur: A certain amount of this water was running over the retaining wall?--Yes.

label: text
text: ABNORMAL RAINFALL

label: text
text: Mr. C. W. Jeffries, acting Director of the Royal Observatory, submitted a report of the rainfall for June and July and asked if he considered it abnormal replied in the affirmative, drawing attention to the fact that a similar quantity had fallen on three previous occasions only, 1885, 1891 and 1892.

label: text
text: Feng Chien, Sanitary foreman, who was at the disinfecting station close by at the time of the disaster, spoke of the, torrents of water washing down from above through a gap in the wall on Maine Road. Questioned, he said that when the old Police station was there, there was a passage for the water.

label: text
text: Sergt. E. Carpenter gave evidence of having noticed prior to the crash water being forced up to a height of three feet through the manhole at the junction of Seymour and Caine Roads. He looked to see where it was finding its way to and suddenly saw the North wall gradually sinking. He saw two or three men rushing out from a matshed on the East. Then the retaining wall on the East gradually fell over. He saw No. 12 Po Hing Fong, gradually sink and the other houses followed it.

label: text
text: The Coroner (Mr. S. B. B. McElderry) decided to adjourn the enquiry until 2:15 p.m. on Monday, and accompanied by the jury, paid another visit to the scene of the disaster.

label: text
text: Mr. F. C. Jenkin attended the enquiry on behalf of five families involved in the catastrophe (the families of Chau Siu-ki, Chu Seng-sang, Chu Chung-how, Wong Pak-san and Chiu Yuk-chow).

label: text
text: The Jury.comprised Captain Thomas Arthur (foreman), Mr. Ho Kom-tong, and Mr. J. O. Sheppard.

label: text
text: Mr. A. G. Tickle, Executive Engineer, P.W.D., submitted his report on the calamity, which was not read.

label: text
text: Norwegian Air Force officer Captain Bruns has arrived at Berlin and submitted to a conference of experts plans for a Zeppelin expedition to the Pole under Nansen in 1927, the route to be from Murmansk and Franz Josofland via the North Pole to Alaska or Anadyr, passing the unexplored areas of the Arctic Ocean to investigate the possibility of establishing regular trans-Arctic air communication between Europe and America via Siberia and Japan. It is estimated that the flight from Murmansk to Anadyr will occupy fifty hours. — Reuter
